corrected_value.title: The N2pc component as an indicator of attentional selectivity
corrected_value.title_o: The N2pc component as an indicator of attentional selectivity

decisions.quote:
This interpretation of the
N2pc component was sparked by the seminal work of Eimer
(1996), which is the target study we attempt to replicate here.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target_index 0) identify the exact same original study: Eimer, M. (1996), 'The N2pc component as an indicator of attentional selectivity', Electroencephalography & Clinical Neurophysiology, 99(3), 225-234 (specifically Experiment 2). The conflicting_dois flag arose only because the manuscript reference list prints the shortDOI 'https://doi.org/dk5b9z', which resolves to the standard Crossref DOI '10.1016/0013-4694(96)95711-9' in the shipped row.

decisions.quote:
We
revisit the idea of the N2pc being an indicator of attentional selectivity by delivering a high
powered direct replication of Eimer’s work through analysis of 779 datasets acquired from 22
labs across 14 countries.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding classify this work as a replication. Primary evidence confirms that 22 laboratories collected 779 new EEG datasets in fresh participant samples to directly re-test Experiment 2 of Eimer (1996).

decisions.quote:
Our results robustly replicate the N2pc to form stimuli, but a direct
replication of the N2pc to color stimuli technically failed.
decisions.reason: With the dependent target identity resolved to Eimer (1996) Experiment 2, both shipped and blind coding agree on a 'mixed' outcome. Across the 22 laboratories in the primary confirmatory ('Original' and 'ICA') pipelines, the authors report that the form N2pc (Hypothesis 1, meta-analytic p < .001) and the amplitude difference between form and color N2pcs (Hypothesis 3, meta-analytic p < .001) robustly replicated in all 22 labs, whereas the direct replication of the color N2pc in the original 220-300 ms window (Hypothesis 2, meta-analytic p > .999) failed to replicate.
